revised_claim: Indonesia has approximately 59 active industrial sugar mills (pabrik gula) producing white crystal sugar (GKP), comprising approximately 40 BUMN-affiliated mills (36 of which are consolidated under PT Sinergi Gula Nusantara, the PTPN III holding subsidiary) and 19 private mills, with a total registered count of ~62 mills (including idled/mothballed units). The vendor-cited figure of 69 is unsubstantiated; the authoritative Kementerian Perindustrian (Kemenperin) figure for 2023 is 59 active mills. Additionally, 11 refining sugar factories (pabrik gula rafinasi / PGR) process imported raw sugar for industrial use; these do not use bagasse-fired boilers in the same way.

mill_count_reconciliation.vendor_blog_figure_69: Unsubstantiated. Likely inflated or counts both GKP mills and PGR (refining) mills together (59 + 11 = 70, near 69).
mill_count_reconciliation.kemenperin_registered_circa_2022: 62 total mills (43 BUMN + 19 private) — ~3 additional BUMN mills likely idled/mothballed
mill_count_reconciliation.sgn_bumn_consolidation: 36 mills under SGN (PTPN III holding) + ~4 more under ID FOOD/RNI holding = ~40 BUMN mills total
mill_count_reconciliation.java_concentration: East Java alone has 30 mills (143,350 TCD). Java overall estimated ~45–48 mills (~75–80% of total). Outer islands (Sumatra + Sulawesi): ~11–14 mills.
mill_count_reconciliation.recommended_figure: 59 active mills (2023 Kemenperin data), with ~62 registered including idled units

boiler_per_mill_estimate.rationale: Indonesian sugar mills are predominantly legacy colonial-era mills (>100 years old per Kemenperin), especially on Java. Most operate a single large bagasse-fired boiler plus one backup/standby unit. Newer private mills in Sulawesi/Sumatra (e.g., Jhonlin Group at 12,000 TCD) may have 2–3 boiler units. SGN's 36 BUMN mills are undergoing revitalization with Rp 12 trillion government program. Conservative range: 59 mills × 1.0–2.0 boilers = 59–118 boilers, midpoint ~80–90.
boiler_per_mill_estimate.capacity_range_per_mill: Average installed capacity ~5,500 TCD/mill (324,350 TCD ÷ 59 mills). Large mills (>6,000 TCD) typically have 2 boilers. Small mills (<3,000 TCD) typically 1 boiler.
boiler_per_mill_estimate.steam_pressure: Typically 20–30 bar for legacy Java mills. Newer outer-island mills 40–60 bar.

notes: The original claim of '69 sugar mills' from zozenboiler.com vendor blog is materially incorrect as a standalone active-mill figure. The most likely explanation: 69 conflates 59 active GKP mills + some fraction of the 11 PGR refining mills, OR uses an older pre-2020 registered count.
The claim should be revised downward to 59 active mills (2023) or ~62 registered mills, with explicit BUMN/private split.

The distinction between GKP mills (bagasse-fired, solid-fuel boilers) and PGR refining mills (no sugarcane crushing, no bagasse — usually gas/fuel oil fired) is critical for the boiler install-base estimate. Only the 59 GKP mills are relevant for solid-fuel package boilers.

BPS sensus industri besar/sedang data was not directly fetchable in this session. The Kemenperin/Badan Pangan Nasional sources are treated as primary-gov (ministry-level) and sufficiently authoritative.

Java vs outer islands split: East Java has 30 mills alone (Badan Pangan data). Remaining Java provinces add ~15–18 more. Outer islands (North Sumatra, South Sumatra, Lampung, South Sulawesi) account for ~11–14 mills, predominantly newer private sector.

The boiler-per-mill multiplier of 1.3 is a judgment call based on mill age profile (most BUMN Java mills are single-boiler colonial-era plants). This should be validated with PTPN/SGN engineering data or Indonesian boiler manufacturer install data.

Confidence rated 'medium' (not 'high') because: (a) Kemenperin article could not be directly fetched — data accessed via cross-reference; (b) no BPS primary census table was retrieved; (c) the exact active/idle split among the 62 registered mills is inferred, not directly stated in fetched sources.
